title: Short Stuff: Animal Politicians
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the long tradition of animals elected or nominated to political office. They cover Milton, Washington's donkey/mule committeeman Boston Curtis; unincorporated towns using pet mayors to raise money, including Omena, Michigan (cat Sweet Tart) and Rabbit Hash, Kentucky (dog Lucy Lou, succeeded by Brenneth Paul Trow); the Texas goat mayors of Lajitas (Clay Henry Sr., Clay Henry Jr., and a third Clay, plagued by beer-drinking and a castration case); animals elected as protest votes against human politicians, such as cat Morris in Mexico, a write-in cat in Alaska, and Cacareco the rhinoceros in Sao Paulo, Brazil in 1959; the Rhinoceros Party in Canada; Pegasus the pig nominated by the Yippies at the 1968 Democratic Convention in Chicago and arrested by police; and Caligula's horse Incitatus, allegedly named consul, possibly a smear story.

segments.title: Opening and animal mayors in Milton, Washington and Michigan
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the idea of animals elected to office. They discuss Milton, Washington's donkey (mule) committeeman Boston Curtis, who was nominated without disclosure, and note that animal candidates usually run in unincorporated towns to raise money.

segments.title: Omena Michigan and Rabbit Hash Kentucky pet mayors
segments.summary: Examples of pet officials used to raise money: Sweet Tart the cat as mayor of Omena, Michigan, with a pet-filled government for the historical society, and Lucy Lou the dog as mayor of Rabbit Hash, Kentucky, succeeded by Brenneth Paul Trow, who ran on restoring the general store.

segments.title: Lajitas Texas goat mayors
segments.summary: The goat mayors of Lajitas, Texas: Clay Henry Sr., who was fed beer at the general store and died after being headbutted by Clay Henry Jr.; a third Clay, also a beer drinker, whose castrator faced animal cruelty charges according to Roadside America.

segments.title: Animals as protest votes against human politicians
segments.summary: Animals elected to shame politicians: cat Morris in Mexico, a write-in cat in Alaska, and Cacareco the rhinoceros who won about 100,000 votes in Sao Paulo, Brazil in 1959. The Rhinoceros Party in Canada followed, a satirical party with a rhino platform.

segments.title: Pegasus the pig at the 1968 Democratic Convention
segments.summary: The Yippies nominated Pegasus the pig for president at the 1968 Democratic Convention in Chicago. Police arrested the pig during a press conference, and it was later placed at an animal society and a farm.

segments.title: Incitatus, Caligula's horse
segments.summary: Caligula's favorite horse Incitatus was reportedly appointed consul to the Roman Senate, though this may be a smear story by political enemies; if true, it would have been meant to humiliate senators.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts encourage voting for animal candidates and end the episode.
